A.explanation: The distance from car to O shortens, so wavefronts are crowded, not stretched. Observed frequency must be greater than $f$, not less than $f$.

B.explanation: The car is approaching O in the radial sense, so frequency is shifted up, not down. The shift also gets smaller, not larger, near Q.

C.explanation: The radial component of car velocity toward O is positive but falls to zero at Q, so observed frequency is above $f$ and decreases toward $f$.

D.explanation: Although frequency starts above $f$, the component of velocity toward O decreases as the car nears Q, so frequency decreases rather than increases.

hints: Notice the dashed line OQ is perpendicular to PQ, so at Q the car moves at right angles to the line joining car and observer, but at P it moves more nearly toward the observer.
Recall Doppler shift for sound depends only on the component of source velocity along the line from source to observer, given by $f_o = f v/(v - v_s)$ where $v_s$ is positive for approach.
Compare the toward-O component $v_s = v \cos\theta$ at P and near Q to decide if the heard frequency is above or below $f$ and whether that shift grows or shrinks.
walkthrough: Identify the geometry: observer O is stationary above Q and PQ is horizontal. As the car moves from P to Q its distance to O decreases, so in the radial sense it is approaching O.

State the Doppler rule: a source approaching the observer crowds wavefronts in the observer direction, giving shorter observed wavelength and observed frequency $f_o = fv/(v-v_s) > f$, where $v_s$ is the component of source speed toward the observer.

Find how $v_s$ changes: $v_s$ is the projection of car speed $v$ onto the source-to-observer direction. At P the source-to-observer line points mostly to the right, so $v_s$ is close to $v$. At Q the line points straight up while velocity points right, so $v_s = 0$.

Connect to frequency trend: large $v_s$ gives large upward shift, small $v_s$ gives small upward shift. Hence $f_o$ starts clearly above $f$ and falls back toward $f$ as the car moves from P toward Q.
This matches a frequency more than $f$ that decreases as the car moves from P towards Q. This is option C
